content.text:
Written to `submission/main.c`. The demo works as follows:

- `low_prio_thread` (prio 10) starts, takes `pi_mutex`, prints "Low: holding mutex", sleeps 300 ms, then releases.
- `med_prio_thread` (prio 7) wakes at 50 ms and loops, printing that it cannot preempt the boosted low-priority holder.
- `high_prio_thread` (prio 4) wakes at 100 ms and blocks on `k_mutex_lock(&pi_mutex, K_FOREVER)` — this is what boosts the low-priority holder to priority 4 via priority inheritance, so the medium thread (7) cannot preempt it. At 300 ms the low thread releases, high acquires, prints "High: acquired mutex", and unlocks.
- `main()` just idles with `k_sleep(K_FOREVER)` since `K_THREAD_DEFINE` threads start automatically.
